evidence.text: The entry classifies 桌 as a phonosemantic graph, 从木、卓声. This supports 木 as the semantic component and 卓 as the sound component in the conventional analysis. It does not establish the historical date or sequence of the graph’s formation.

evidence.text: The entry describes 桌 as both an ideographic and phono-semantic compound, with 卓 as phonetic and 木 as semantic, and supplies a Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese comparison. This is a secondary account and its proposed graph history is not independently established by dated early 桌 forms in the sources inspected.

evidence.text: The Ministry dictionary reports historical furniture spellings 倚卓 and 倚棹, cites 楊億《談苑》 for 檀香倚卓 in the 咸平、景德 reign periods (998–1007), and treats 棹 as a variant for the furniture sense. This is a report of textual evidence, not proof that the graph 桌 itself occurs in that early passage; it distinguishes 棹/櫂 in its oar sense as another history.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》：A01921 桌

evidence.source: 澎湃新闻 / 雅昌艺术网, 张辉
evidence.text: The author reports the name 卓子 in 楊億《談苑》 for the 998–1007 period, cites Southern Song 棹 examples in 朱子語類 and 建炎以来系年要录, and says 卓 and 棹 were both used in Song, Yuan, and Ming. The article reports 明末《正字通》 as an early dictionary recording of 桌, with “俗呼几案曰桌.” These are secondary reports of textual attestations, not a comprehensive search proving first use.
evidence.title: 雅昌专栏 | 张辉：唐宋时期局脚桌流变——《中国家具史》

gaps: No dated early form of the graph 桌 was established by the inspected pages. The early furniture word/orthography reported as 倚卓/倚棹 is separate evidence from the later dictionary entry 桌.

The reported semantic motivation ‘high’ from 卓 is a plausible naming account, but the evidence inspected does not prove that the word originated by combining 木 and 卓 or establish a precise graphic sequence. The claim that 卓’s 十 merged with or was replaced by 木 remains unsupported here.
No classifier-use chronology or proven pathway from table noun to a classifier was established.

The proposed original referent and original name/pronunciation of any object depicted by early 卓 forms remain unresolved; no such object-name premise is needed to support 卓 as a phonetic component in the later 桌 analysis.

The exact Unihan official URLs for 桌 and 卓 were attempted, but the live pages failed to open. Exact current Mandarin readings are reported from the provided local Unihan table rows; there is no external click-through verification in this run.

No source license or reuse grant for recurring dictionary text was checked; no local extract is recommended. Commons image rights apply to the modern vector files only, not to database or dictionary text.

items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 卓 in bronze-script style. It illustrates an early form tradition for the phonetic element discussed in 桌, but does not show an attested early 桌 or prove how 桌 was formed.
items.alt: Black bronze-script-style graph 卓 on a white background.
items.selection_reason: Shows a source-described ancient script form of 卓, the independently analyzed sound component; Commons identifies the Hanziyuan source image and declares this SVG representation public domain.
items.rights: Commons declares the vector representation public domain; the description credits the Hanziyuan source image B12552 and cites permission from Richard Sears.

items.period: Seal-script style; no specific artifact date is supplied
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 卓 in a seal-script style associated with Shuowen. It is a later script-style reference, not a photograph of an excavated object or evidence for the date of 桌.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style graph 卓 on a white background.
items.selection_reason: Offers a clearly labeled later graphic reference to compare with the bronze-style rendering; source page identifies the character and public-domain status of the vector.

limitations.text: Commons description pages identify these as modern vector redrawings based on Hanziyuan image records. The proposed image candidates are not photographs of inscribed artifacts, and no image pixels were visually inspected in this research stage.
The source image pages concern 卓, not 桌. They can illustrate the proposed phonetic component’s script history but cannot demonstrate an early 桌 graph or confirm a merge of 卓’s 十 with 木.
